claims.text: Machine-learning-driven optimization of thermomechanical processing can systematically tune microstructural features in non-equiatomic HEAs.
Tuning microstructural features through optimized processing can enhance the magnetic response of non-equiatomic HEAs.
Tuning microstructural features through optimized processing can enhance the magnetocaloric response of non-equiatomic HEAs.
The proposed magnetic and magnetocaloric tuning does not require changes in alloy composition.
Annealing temperature can be correlated with grain size or phase fraction in the target HEAs.
Strain rate can be correlated with grain size or phase fraction in the target HEAs.
Dimensional constraints can be correlated with grain size or phase fraction in the target HEAs.
Machine-learning-guided annealing and thermomechanical schedules can refine the grain structure.
Machine-learning-guided processing can alter magnetic domain architecture.
Refined grain structure and altered domain architecture can control magnetic transition temperatures.
Optimized thermomechanical pathways influence magnetic domain size.
Optimized thermomechanical pathways influence phase distribution.
Optimized thermomechanical pathways influence defect density.
Changes in domain size, phase distribution, and defect density affect magnetic transition behavior and the magnetocaloric effect.
Machine-learning-optimized processing will produce a larger magnetic entropy change near the transition temperature than conventional unoptimized processing.
